subject: Acme: auth gateway error spike — misclassified 5xx/429 + retry spiral
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Spike of 5xx/429 affecting our customers — can you triage?

Hi Hannah,

We are seeing a major spike in 5xx and 429 responses to calls against /v1/generate and /v1/chat starting ~15:55 UTC. Customer-facing requests are timing out and then our clients are retrying aggressively, which is amplifying the load.

Sample: we attached a small dump (acme_error_samples.txt) with response headers and a couple of request ids. A few lines from the dump:
- 2026-12-11T15:57:22Z POST /v1/generate -> 502, gateway: "timeout after 10s"
- 2026-12-11T15:58:10Z POST /v1/chat -> 429, x-rate-limit: "exceeded"
- Some requests show "token validation failed" in body but the returned code is 429/502.

We suspect something in the auth/token path is involved — several of our failed requests had an Authorization: Bearer <JWT> header. We haven't made changes on our end. Can your team confirm if there was a change/deploy in the auth gateway or rate-limiter?

This is impacting several enterprise customers; we're escalating on our side as well. Please advise on immediate mitigations we can apply (e.g., temporarily disabling client-side retries, or a token-leeway tweak).

Thanks,
James
Product Ops — Acme Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: James Lee <james.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx/429 affecting our customers — can you triage?

Hi James — thanks for the heads up and the sample file. I’m escalating to engineering and CS now.

Immediate asks:
- If possible, can you temporarily disable aggressive client-side retries for the affected environments? Even a short window with retries off will help isolate the issue.
- Can you confirm whether the tokens were issued >10 minutes earlier (we want to check clock skew/expiry)?

I’ve looped in Marissa and Sergio from CS — they’ll coordinate customer comms while Rishi takes the lead on engineering triage. I’ll follow up with ETA within 30 minutes.

— Hannah
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:44:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Internal: Acme 5xx/429 spike — root cause & mitigations in flight

Quick summary of findings (initial):
- Root cause chain appears to be twofold: (1) a validation path in auth-proxy is misclassifying token parse/validation errors as transient upstream errors which causes us to treat them like internal failures; and (2) a client retry pattern from multiple Acme customers (short backoff, high fanout) produced a retry spiral that saturated our gateway queues.

Evidence:
- Logs for request ids in acme_error_samples.txt show "jwt: parse error" and "nbf/exp out-of-range" entries for many of the failed requests, but the auth-proxy returned 502/429 to callers instead of a 401/403.
- Rate-limiter metrics show a 12x increase in queued requests and CPU on gateway pods spiked, causing timeouts and subsequent 502s.
- There was a light clock-drift event in one issuing region earlier this morning; some JWTs had nbf timestamps that were slightly in the future relative to gateway node clocks (we have metric gaps showing a handful of nodes with up to 95s skew).

Immediate mitigations applied (in flight):
1) Hotfix pushed to auth-proxy to correctly map token validation failures to 401/403 rather than counting them as internal errors. Rolling to 30% of gateway pods now; target 100% in 45–60m. (patch: auth-proxy-mitigation.patch)
2) Temporary rate-limiter rule: treat 401s from auth-proxy as non-accountable (do not increment burst counters) and reduce immediate throttling for Acme traffic. Deployed as a scoped rule for acme-analytics client_id.
3) Increase JWT clock-leeway on gateway from 30s -> 150s as a temporary tolerance during rollout to avoid rejecting slightly skewed tokens.
4) We’ve asked Acme to disable client-side retries for 30 minutes (they confirmed).

Impact so far: error rate has dropped ~60% on scoped traffic after 2nd mitigation, overall queue depth is declining. Full resolution depends on completing the auth-proxy rollout.

Follow-ups required:
- Postmortem (root cause: misclassification + clock skew + retry behavior)
- Persisted observability: split metric streams for auth-failures vs internal gateway failures; tracing to include auth-failure reason.
- Update SDKs and developer docs to recommend jittered exponential backoff and token-leeway recommendations.

Rishi
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: James Lee <james.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx/429 affecting our customers — can you triage?

Hi James — quick update from our side: thanks again for the samples.

What we found and what we’ve done so far:
- Cause: an auth validation path was incorrectly surfaced as internal errors for certain JWT parse/validation failures; combined with a small set of gateway nodes exhibiting ~1–2 minute clock skew, some tokens were being treated as invalid. That + aggressive client retries produced a retry spiral that amplified the problem.
- Mitigations in flight: corrected mapping in auth-proxy (rolling out now), temporary increase to token clock-leeway, and scoped rate-limiter rule for your client_id to avoid penalizing auth failures.
- Impact: We’ve seen a ~60% reduction in client-scoped errors; overall system queues are returning to normal.

Next steps / ETA:
- Hotfix rollout to complete within ~45–60 minutes.
- We will follow with a short postmortem and a list of actions (patch, SDK guidance, monitoring changes) within 48 hours.

We’ll also propose a goodwill usage credit for the affected window; Marissa will coordinate offline with your billing contact.

Hannah
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident summary: Acme auth/gateway error spike (5xx/429) — actions & next steps

Executive summary:
- Between 15:55–17:10 UTC on 2026-12-11 we observed an elevated 5xx/429 error rate impacting traffic from Acme Analytics and several other customers. Root cause: token validation failures were misclassified as gateway/internal errors (auth-proxy mapping bug), exacerbated by localized node clock skew and aggressive client retry behavior which generated a retry storm.

Actions completed:
- Hotfix to auth-proxy deployed (complete rollout by 17:30 UTC). See patch: auth-proxy-mitigation.patch (attached).
- Scoped rate-limiter rule deployed for acme-analytics client_id; 401s are not counted against burst consumption.
- Temporary JWT clock-leeway increased to 150s for affected gateway region — revert plan in postmortem.
- Customer communications sent and goodwill credit proposed.

Remaining items / owners / ETA:
- Rishi: Postmortem write-up and monitoring split for auth failures vs internal errors — due 2026-12-13 EOD.
- Tessa: SDK/backoff guidance doc + client library patch (recommend jitter + capped retries) — due 2026-12-17.
- Sergio & Marissa: finalize customer credits and outbound comms — due 2026-12-14.

Preliminary lessons:
- Authentication failures must be categorized distinctly in metrics and not treated as internal failures that count toward rate-limiter throttles.
- Add automated checks for node clock drift during rollouts and make token-leeway a dynamic config per region.

Attached: incident_timeline.pdf (timeline + key logs), auth-proxy-mitigation.patch

Hannah Schmitt
Principal Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
